notes: The manual excerpt only says the PIR has three pins that connect to the Raspberry Pi. It doesn't say which pins to use or show a wiring diagram.
I assumed the usual wiring for this Raspberry Pi PIR project: VCC to 5V, GND to GND, and OUT to GPIO14. GPIO14 is a guess. Any free GPIO pin would work.
The PIR pins are male and the Pi header is male, so female-to-female jumper wires are needed. The catalogue has no female-to-female type, so I used the generic jumper-wire.
The PIR is connected directly to the Pi's header with no breadboard.
